_source: I-SAPS 'Novice Level Reading Resources edited (1).docx' (partner-supplied edited list, Oct 2026; replaces the Sept 2026 95-item list). Items with url null are listed by I-SAPS as 'Free resource not available'.

1.title: Changing Education Paradigms — TED Talk / RSA Animate (2010)
1.author: Sir Ken Robinson
1.description: A systemic critique of factory-model schooling and conventional approaches to education.

1.title: The New Meaning of Educational Change (5th ed., 2015)
1.author: Michael Fullan
1.description: Explores why meaningful educational transformation requires systemic thinking rather than isolated fixes at the individual teacher level.

1.title: Professional Capital (2012)
1.author: Andy Hargreaves and Michael Fullan
1.description: Argues for building teacher professional capacity within realistic system constraints.

2.title: The Beautiful Risk of Education (2013)
2.author: Gert Biesta
2.description: Explores the idea of subjectification: education as supporting students in developing voice, agency, and the capacity to think for themselves.

2.title: The Power of Yet (2014)
2.author: Carol Dweck
2.description: Carol S. Dweck is a leading researcher in the field of motivation and is the Lewis and Virginia Eaton Professor of Psychology at Stanford. Her research focuses on why students succeed and how to foster their success. More specifically, her work has demonstrated the role of mindsets in success and has shown how praise for intelligence can undermine students’ motivation and learning.

2.title: Those Who Understand: Knowledge Growth in Teaching (1986)
2.author: Lee Shulman
2.description: Introduces the concept of Pedagogical Content Knowledge (PCK), highlighting the importance of understanding how students engage with and respond to specific subject content.

2.title: Structured Classroom Management Research (2022)
2.author: Wilkins
2.description: Explores pre-emptive participation design and the role of clear expectations in increasing classroom engagement.

2.title: “Grit: The Power of Passion and Perseverance” — TED Talk (2013)
2.author: Angela Duckworth
2.description: Explores the role of persistence and the conditions that shape sustained effort.

3.title: Impact of Classroom Management Control on the Academic Performance of Students: Basis for Instructional Enhancement
3.author: Roselyn D. Ramo
3.description: This study examines the relationship between teachers' classroom management control and students’ academic performance, focusing on key indicators such as withitness, overlapping, smoothness and momentum, group focus, and behavior management.

3.title: “Teaching: The Greatest Job in the World” — TEDx Talk (2015)
3.author: Joe Ruhl
3.description: Explores teacher burnout and the factors that can make classroom teaching energising or exhausting.

4.title: Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge: A Framework for Teacher Knowledge (2006)
4.author: Punya Mishra and Matthew Koehler
4.description: The original paper introducing the TPACK framework.

4.title: “Let's Use Video to Reinvent Education” — TED Talk (2011)
4.author: Sal Khan
4.description: Explores how technology can transform learning when used intentionally rather than decoratively.

4.title: TPACK Explained
4.author: Matthew J. Koehler
4.description: A visual overview of the three knowledge domains within TPACK and their intersection.

5.title: Introduction to Assessment
5.author: Kingsborough Community College
5.description: Introduces the basic purposes, concepts, and processes of assessment.

5.title: Defining Assessment
5.author: University of Michigan, Center for Research on Learning and Teaching
5.description: Defines assessment and distinguishes formative, summative, and authentic assessment approaches.

5.title: The Assessment Cycle Step-by-Step
5.author: University of West Florida
5.description: Step-by-step guide to identifying learning outcomes, selecting assessment methods, collecting evidence, and using results.

6.title: The Beautiful Risk of Education (2013)
6.author: Gert Biesta
6.description: Explores the relationship between teaching and learning, arguing for keeping them apart and suggesting that learning may not be the one and only option for teaching to aim for.

6.title: “The Linguistic Genius of Babies” — TED Talk (2010)
6.author: Patricia Kuhl
6.description: Explores how expectations and environments shape cognitive development.

6.title: Active Learning
6.author: Edutopia
6.description: A video resource on active learning approaches.

6.title: Learner-Centered Classroom
6.author: Sociology Burger
6.description: A video resource exploring learner-centred teaching and learning.

7.title: Teachers Who Dare Teach — Pedagogy of Hope (1994)
7.author: Paulo Freire
7.description: Explores qualities and virtues associated with teaching, including humility, tolerance, decisiveness, and joy.

7.title: The Global Achievement Gap (2008)
7.author: Tony Wagner
7.description: Introduces the Seven Survival Skills, including critical thinking, collaboration, and effective communication, which inform the 5Cs framework.

7.title: The Conditions of Learning (1985)
7.author: Robert Gagné
7.description: Introduces the Nine Events of Instruction, a foundational framework for structured lesson sequencing.

7.title: “Creating Innovators” — Google Talk (2012)
7.author: Tony Wagner
7.description: Explores why twenty-first-century skills should move beyond knowledge transmission as a central goal of schooling.

8.title: Teach Like a Champion vs an Enquiry Approach – Is There a Middle Ground? (2023)
8.author: Therese Andrews and Emma Oliver
8.description: Argues that presenting traditional and progressive teaching as opposites is a false dichotomy, and describes an enquiry curriculum in which teachers guide students through structured enquiries using Teach Like a Champion techniques.

8.title: Expanding preservice teachers' metacognitive awareness of instructional planning through pedagogical agents (2002)
8.author: Amy L. Baylor
8.description: An experimental study of 135 preservice teachers in which constructivist and instructivist mentor agents changed how they thought about, and wrote, instructional plans.

9.title: Leaders Mentoring Others: The Effects of Implicit Followership Theory on Leader Integrity and Mentoring
9.author: Jeffrey Yip and Dayna O. H. Walker
9.description: Examines how leaders’ assumptions about followers relate to leader integrity, engagement, and mentoring effectiveness.

9.title: How to Break Through Fear and Become a Leader
9.author: Valerie Montgomery Rice
9.description: TED Talk on vigilance, grit, resilience, overcoming fear, and leadership.

9.title: Teacher Leader Model Standards
9.author: Teacher Leadership Exploratory Consortium
9.description: Standards describing seven domains of teacher leadership, including collaboration, professional learning, assessment/data use, and advocacy.
